title: Hair loss during chemotherapy: preparation and support
intro: Some chemotherapy damages rapidly dividing hair-producing cells. Hair loss varies by medicine and dose and may involve the scalp, eyebrows, lashes and body. It does not show whether treatment is working or how serious the cancer is.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Ask what is likely with your specific regimen before treatment begins. Hair often regrows after treatment, sometimes with changed texture or color, but timing varies and persistent thinning can occur.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: The oncology team can distinguish expected hair loss from scalp infection or another cause. Report tenderness, sores and unusual skin changes, and ask whether planned medicines make any scalp products unsuitable. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Scalp cooling may reduce hair loss with some regimens but is unsuitable for some cancers and is not guaranteed. Discuss availability, discomfort and limitations before treatment; avoid unapproved hair-growth products or supplements. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Use gentle washing and brushing, protect exposed scalp from sun and cold, and avoid harsh chemicals or excessive heat. Wigs, scarves, hats or leaving the head uncovered are personal choices; emotional support is legitimate care. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Ask the team about regrowth expectations and persistent hair loss after treatment. Fever or a painful red scalp during chemotherapy requires prompt advice using the oncology emergency plan, rather than cosmetic treatment alone.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira chooses a scarf and asks about a wig before treatment. Planning gives her options without implying that covering hair loss is compulsory.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben asks whether scalp cooling suits his chemotherapy. He weighs likely benefit and discomfort without assuming it can preserve every hair.
